newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bullion pulled down by world trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian bullion pulled down by world trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 15 rupees lower at 4,835 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,850 rupees as setbacks in the world market prompted profit-taking while fresh seasonal buying remained dull at the higher level.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 56,600 rupees per piece after a gain of 100 rupees on Monday. They were up by 1,100 rupees per piece last week.

** Silver (.999) closed 15 rupees lower at 7,080 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,095 rupees on the back of fresh arrivals of imported metals while a slide in the world market triggered unloading by the local stockists. Silver was up by 15 rupees per kg on Monday.

Gold 24 carat closed 15 rupees lower at 4,835 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,850 rupees as demand resistance capped the recent rally while a setback in the world market drove local prices downward, dealers said.
Gold was up by 10 rupees per 10 gramme on Monday and by 90 rupees last week.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 56,600 rupees per piece after a gain of 100 rupees on Monday. They were up by 1,100 rupees per piece last week.

Silver (.999) closed 15 rupees lower at 7,080 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,095 rupees on the back of fresh arrivals of about 1,500/2,000 kg of imported silver while demand resistance and the slide in the world market prompted profit-taking.
Silver was up by 15 rupees per kg on Monday and by 275 rupees per kg during last week.
Overall market sentiment for both precious metals remained subdued at the close of the session. (Conversion $1=35.83 rupees)
